newsitem.title: UK: POUND SEEN HITTING SMITH & NEPHEW H1 PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: POUND SEEN HITTING SMITH & NEPHEW H1 PROFIT.

text.p: Healthcare group Smith & Nephew Plc is expected to report a drop of about 11 percent in its first-half profits, which are due on Tuesday.
Adverse currency movements will have been the main factor depressing results, analysts said.
They predict pre-tax profits to fall to 79-81.5 million stg from 90.8 million stg a year ago.
Currencies, such as the pound, will have wiped about 10 million stg off the first-half results, industry watchers said.
They also pointed to the strengthening of the dollar versus many European currencies. This means a higher cost base for Smith & Nephew, while income is under pressure at the same time.
"The collapse of European currencies means there is a mismatch between the cost base and some of the sales areas," said Stephen Putnam at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
To a lesser extent, Smith & Nephew's imminent introduction later this year of its skin graft product Dermagraft will have also weighed on the interim results as launch costs start to come in.
Finally, Smith & Nephew is also suffering from price pressure in the U.S., especially in the orthopaedic implants business.
Despite the this gloom, several analysts are bullish on Smith & Nephew as they believe the potential of Dermagraft is not reflected in the share price.
Dermagraft will turn Smith & Nephew into a high-tech, high-margin group, which should deserve a higher market rating, Smith & Nephew's backers said.
In a recent note, analysts at Salomon Brothers set a 12-month price target of 200 pence, compared with a current share price of 174-1/2 pence.
